description-proc.eng: The object of this procurement is the delivery of satellite orthomosaic images to the National Land Survey of Finland ("NLS") . The production areas to be ordered are based on the national laser scanning and aerial imaging programme. The procurement includes the delivery of 10 production areas (3 priority 1 production areas and 7 priority 2 production areas) which are defined in more detail in Appendix 1 Technical requirements and Appendix 1.1 Production areas. This procurement forms part of the NLS' preparedness for the situation where aerial images cannot be obtained from all production areas due to GNSS interference. Therefore, the procurement also includes the possibility to order maximum of 5 additional production areas (priority 3 production areas). The production areas from which these priority 3 production areas are selected are indicated in Section 4 of the Appendix 1. NLS does not commit to purchasing any priority 3 production areas from the supplier under this procurement. If NLS orders priority 3 production areas, the supplier shall have the right to refuse to accept such orders. The object of the procurement and the production areas are described in more detail in Appendix 1 and Appendix 1.1. See also chapters 10 and 11 of the Appendix A Contract. TERM OF THE CONTRACT The contract enters into force upon signature. The objective is that the contract will be signed by the end of February 2027. description: The objective of this framework contract is to operate the CEMS "Hydrological Forecast Centre - Computation" (COMP) service in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. The role of COMP is to execute the flood forecasts for EFAS and GloFAS and hosts the different data dissemination and visualization platforms. The framework contract is a follow up of an existing framework contract 941462-IPR-2021. The CEMS implementation is an inter-service arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO (Ares (2021) 2234141). The JRC is in charge of preparing and implements the CEMS work programmes, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.
